title: Add RAG Lab Notebook: compact workshop, offline eval kit, and snippet curator
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds a compact RAG lab notebook quickstart with an offline eval harness, snippet curator UI for authoring test prompts, and telemetry preset examples for local dev.
description: Summary: Introduce a compact, local-first RAG Lab Notebook quickstart designed for developer onboarding, authoring reproducible prompt/eval suites, and running offline evals against seeded corpora. Motivation: teams repeatedly ask for a small dev-friendly sandbox that combines interactive authoring (notebook + curator), a repeatable offline eval runner (so you can run batches locally without the full infra), and telemetry presets to match Redwood Console naming conventions. This quickstart reduces the time to iterate on prompt variants and catch regressions in retrieval+generation setups. What this PR adds: 1) rag-lab-notebook/ - Jupyter-compatible notebook with step-by-step authoring flow, compact dataset fixtures, and example retrieval adapters for local SQLite indexes. 2) offline-eval/ - small harness (python) to run deterministic evals against a seeded corpus, produces JSONL results and a small HTML summary. 3) snippet-curator/ - tiny React page used by the notebook that lets authors tag prompt/test pairs and export them as eval fixtures. 4) telemetry-presets.yaml - example telemetry naming conventions and probe hooks to ensure events line up with Redwood Console dashboards. 5) contract-templates/ - typed tool-contract examples (TS + JSON Schema) demonstrating how to declare tool shape for the notebook's tool-calling examples. Why this is different: unlike the larger workshop kits we already have, this is intentionally compact (<100MB), offline-first, and targeted at iterative authoring cycles where engineers want to run quick regressions locally before pushing to CI or Dedicated. Checklist (author): - [x] Notebook walkthrough with inline assertions and expected outputs - [x] Offline eval harness and example seed corpus - [x] Snippet curator UI + export/import of fixtures - [x] Telemetry presets that mirror production naming - [x] Tests: smoke CI for notebook kernel and offline-eval runner - [x] Docs site entry and short README in quickstart folder Usage notes: - Start: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt - Launch notebook: make start-notebook - Run offline eval: ./offline-eval/run_eval.py --fixtures fixtures/seed.jsonl --output results/out.jsonl - Snippet curator runs as a dev server (cd snippet-curator && yarn && yarn start) Migration/impact: No breaking changes. The telemetry presets are examples only and do not affect production. The contract templates are additive and safe to import. Related: closes ENG-4392 (authoring seedkit) and partially implements PM-118 (developer ramp). Links: docs-site PR (coming: link to redwood-docs entry), demo recording uploaded to Linear. Implementation notes: - The offline-eval harness intentionally avoids network calls and uses an in-memory simulated retrieval adapter to ensure deterministic behavior. - The snippet-curator is tiny (no backend) and uses localStorage for fixtures to keep the quickstart self-contained. Security: no secrets are committed; sample KMS placeholders are documented. Compatibility: works with Redwood SDKs (Python/TS) pinned to 2025.11 compat range. Next steps: - Add a CI job to run offline-eval nightly against a small regression set - Wire exported fixtures into centralized eval runner for cross-team comparisons - Expand telemetry presets to include token-level breakdowns Examples and snippets are included in the notebook; the README contains step-by-step troubleshooting tips for common kernel issues.
